title: Reproducing Rabie, Haddara and Carette 2005: a kinetic model of SiGe oxidation against four wet oxidations

sample.paper: “a SiGe sample with 14% Ge” (LeGoues); “SiGe samples having 28% and 36% Ge” (Liu); “50% Ge” (Zhang). Called “the original epilayer” for Liu
sample.ours: FAMILY: SiGe_oxide; COMPOSITION: Si0.86Ge0.14 | Si0.72Ge0.28 | Si0.64Ge0.36 | Si0.50Ge0.50
an infinite alloy, as in the paper's model
sample.note: Whether the alloy could be consumed through is unknown: Table VI gives up to 425 nm of alloy consumed in the Liu cases.

sample.paper: “a SiyGe1-y layer covered by a layer of oxide of very small thickness Lox” (the model's initial condition; no number)
sample.ours: L_0 = 1 nm, a hypothesis inside the program
sample.note: A property of the sample held as a parameter of the program; the history cannot state it.

history.paper: not stated: Rabie et al. give only the germanium fraction, the temperature and the gas of each experiment they model
history.ours: CLEAN: not_stated; no epilayer thickness, strain or substrate
history.note: The alloy is treated as an infinite substrate of constant composition, as in the paper's model.

history.ours: RUN Push DURATION 60 TEMP 600->800 AMBIENT mix:H2O=0.55,O2=0.45
history.note: A push of one minute from 200 °C below the oxidation temperature, in the oxidation gas. Ours, not the paper's: it stands for the time the wafer spends heating before the clock of the figure starts.

history.paper: “LeGoues et al. used wet oxygen to oxidize a SiGe sample with 14% Ge at 800 °C. The oxide obtained was pure SiO2. A 50-nm-thick Ge-rich layer was obtained with up to 75% Ge.”
history.ours: RUN Oxidation DURATION 10800 TEMP 800->800 AMBIENT mix:H2O=0.55,O2=0.45
history.note: Wet oxygen is written as 55% steam and 45% oxygen at 1 atm: the steam fraction that Rabie's own C* for wet oxygen implies (Table IV against Table II). The paper gives no pressure, flow or bubbler temperature. The Rabie program does not read the gas; the inventory program does.

history.ours: the history ends when the oxidation ends

history.paper: “Our simulation results for the oxide thickness are in excellent agreement with the measurements as shown in Figs. 3-5.”
history.note: The technique is the original authors'; Rabie et al. do not name it.

history.paper: Table III: k1, k2, k3 chosen for each experiment (“free parameters”); Table V: DSiGe for each experiment
history.ours: the LeGoues constants for every history
history.note: Only the LeGoues row is in the program. The predictor runs it for 700 °C steam and 1000 °C wet oxygen without a label.
